newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw WIG 20 index to update during session.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw WIG 20 index to update during session.

text.p: The Polish bourse will start in January to show updates in the WIG 20 index of large-cap, liquid stocks during the continuous trade session, the bourse's president said on Friday.
"We expect that in January the WIG 20 index will be counted in real time, probably in five-minute intervals," Wieslaw Rozlucki told Reuters.
At present, fluctuations in the WIG 20 index are announced only once daily, after the regular bourse session.

Bourse deputy president Piotr Szeliga said the WIG 20 level would be announced after the single-price-auction session's fixing, when the main WIG index fixing is also set, and would be able to end the day after continuous trade at a different level.
The Warsaw bourse has introduced continuous trading in 15 of the main board's 83 companies and all the stocks in the WIG 20 index will be part of this system by January 2.
Starting on Monday, six more stocks will enter continuous trading, bringing the total to 21.
The bourse already plans on January 2 to lengthen its sessions by an hour and a half, with sessions lasting from 1100 until 1430 local time.
In January continuous trade will begin after the regular single-price-auction session ends, instead of the two running concurrently as they do now.

For stocks trading in both systems the price at the single-price-auction system will be the starting point for the continuous trade system. The regular bourse session will begin at 1100 local time and end at 1200.
The bourse changes its WIG 20 line-up every quarter.
